issues.reason: TimesAs takes an exact factor ('twice' -> 2), so (TimesAs amount sk_thing_1 sk_quarter_1 2) asserts the figure WAS double — which 'more than double' denies — putting a false, over-precise claim in the KB; gap territory does not excuse a false atom.

The half that stands: a Measure's scale is a dimension, and $102 million and 13 cents-a-share are different dimensions, so sharing the symbol `amount` makes the KB read two conflicting values on one scale; the half that falls: each atom is individually true of the sentence and the appositional equivalence has no licensed carrier (the reviewer's own gap 2), so the only available 'fix' would be a second invented scale word or the loss of a true figure.

The scale rule enumerates its cases — the stated gradable adjective, else the dimension noun — and the fragment supplies neither, which the reviewer registers as its own gap 3; the slot is mandatory, and the generic `amount` is true of the content and well-typed, so this is licensed improvisation rather than a rule violation.

The 'night_shift is not night' rule bars exposing a modifier as the genus of a FUSED compound; the parse did not fuse but took the 'dented pail' split for a non-classifying modifier — (Member sk_pail_1 pail) (Member sk_pail_1 dented) — and 'year-earlier' is predicable of the quarter, so nothing false or ill-typed is emitted.

gaps_confirmed: bounded multiplicative comparative ('more than double', 'at least twice as many') — TimesAs takes an exact factor with no AtLeast/AtMost counterpart, unlike Cardinality and Measure

appositional 'or' restating one value in a second denomination ('the $102 million, or 13 cents a share') — an equivalence, not a disjunction, and no construction records that two measures denote the same quantity
a bare currency figure with no stated dimension word ('the $102 million for the quarter') — the Measure scale rule needs a surface adjective or dimension noun and neither is present
